summary: Midday dedicated pool thin GPU supply during tenant sweep — autoscaler missed short-lived noisy background job
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported a sudden midday drop in end-to-end throughput (p50/p95 unchanged, p99 spiked) for their dedicated pool between 11:18–11:42 UTC. Requests were queuing; autoscaler did not add capacity during the window. We observed a simultaneous burst of short-lived background jobs from the customer that performed heavy NVMe writes (checkpoint/upload sweep). Hypothesis: NVMe/PCIe IO burst from a noisy background writer caused attach latencies and ephemeral GPU slot hold, which the autoscaler sensors treat as transient and ignored, leading to a thin effective GPU supply and elevated queueing.

Impact:
- Customer NarrativeAI experienced ~45% throughput degradation on batched routes for 24 minutes (11:18–11:42 UTC).
- P99 latency for their ticketed routes rose from ~120ms to ~1.8s.
- Autoscaler did not react due to hysteresis and sensor filtering; several attach attempts timed out and triggered requeue loops.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-narrative-prod-us-east-1 (reserved, dedicated GPUs).
- Cluster flavor: a100-80gb-hetero; scheduler v2.3.1; autoscaler v1.9.0; runtime 2026.02.11-release.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer runs checkpoint-sweep job across many small files using their snapshotter concurrently with live inference traffic.
2) Snapshotter generates high NVMe write IOPS + PCIe bursts on nodes hosting the dedicated pool.
3) Serving runtime attach attempts experience increased NVMe ioctl/attach latency and occasional EBUSY from device; prefetch/pinning takes longer.
4) Autoscaler sensors see short attach flaps but their smoothing window suppresses scale-up.
5) Requests queue; throughput drops and latency spikes.

Notes: This is not a model regression; model CPU/GPU compute did not appear to be the bottleneck. Symptoms point to IO noise and autoscaler detection thresholds that treat momentary attach noise as transient rather than actionable.
steps_to_reproduce: Run many small-file snapshot uploads from tenant nodes while sending batched inference traffic to dedicated pool
Observe NVMe write IOPS spike and attach latency rising in serving logs
Watch autoscaler sensor smoothing prevent scale-up despite rising attach failures

comments: 2026-03-13 | Jordan Patel: Customer reporting sustained throughput loss; p99 spike, autoscaler didn't scale. Assigned to SRE for immediate triage.
2026-03-13 | Avery Chen: Observed NVMe/io spikes on nodes correlated with customer snapshotter activity. Reproduced short attach timeouts. Opening scheduler/attach traces.

2026-03-13 | Samira Ortiz (SRE): Temporarily applied workaround: reduce batch_size to 2 for ticketed routes and enabled sticky-evict for snapshotter namespaces to lower concurrent IO pressure. Requesting engineering follow-up for autoscaler sensitivity.
2026-03-14 | Customer (NarrativeAI): Confirmed throughput recovered after we applied the workaround; they'll delay snapshot sweep and investigate bursting behavior in their pipeline.
investigation_notes: Correlation found between high NVMe write IOPS on shared nodes and attach latency in serving runtime
Autoscaler sensor uses a 5m smoothing window with a 0.2 attach error threshold; raw attach error rate briefly exceeded 0.15 but smoothing prevented action
Observed EBUSY and ioctl timeouts from kernel logs during burst window; disk queue depth and PCIe latency spikes present
Gremlin test: simulated 30s NVMe write burst caused attach latencies and prevented scale-up in current autoscaler config
Hypothesis: short-lived noisy snapshotter jobs hold prefetch/prefetch leases and cause a cascade of attach retries that appear ephemeral to smoothed sensors
resolution_notes:
Mitigation applied (2026-03-13 12:05 UTC):
- Customer delayed snapshot sweep and reduced concurrency.
- Support temporarily lowered batch sizes for affected routes and enabled sticky-evict for snapshotter namespaces on their dedicated pool.
- SRE opened an infra change to adjust autoscaler sensitivity for IO-related attach errors (see related PR).

Permanent follow-up actions (roadmap):
- Autoscaler: introduce an 'io-noise' detection signal and short-window emergency scale path to react to attach-time anomalies without long smoothing delays.
- Scheduler: add prefetch lease timeout telemetry and eviction policy to preempt long-held snapshot leases.
- Runbook: update 'dedicated pool noisy IO' runbook with steps to identify snapshotter patterns and recommend tenant-level throttles.
Owner: Avery Chen (autoscaler follow-up), Samira Ortiz (scheduler/eviction work), Jordan Patel (customer liaison)
